notes.bwe: For real situations: Bwe nzuukuka… When I wake up…

guidebook.intro: Real situations take **bwe** (when, if). Imagined ones take **singa** (if) and the conditional **-andi-** (would).

tips.title: When: bwe
body: Put **bwe** before the verb for “when” or “whenever”: **Bwe nzuukuka** (when I wake up), **Bwe ntuuka** (when I arrive). With a noun, it goes after the noun and joins the verb: **Enkuba bw’etonya** (when the rain falls).

tips.title: If: singa and -andi-
body: For things that aren’t true, start with **singa** and put the result in the conditional with **-andi-**: **nandiguze** (I would buy), **nandigenze** (I would go), **wandiguze** (you would buy).
**Nandyagade** (I would like) is the politest way to ask for something: **Nandyagade caayi**.

culture.title: God willing
body: You met **Katonda bw’anaayagala** in Unit 20. It literally means “if God wants”, built with **bwe**, and follows almost every promise about the future.
